source.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
source.authors: Sambit Ghosh; Madelyn Mathai; R. Babu; Chirag Agarwal

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present. Some equations and tables have minor extraction/layout artifacts, but the feature-correspondence results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It measures one-to-one SAE feature correspondence across activation budgets, a different empirical test of whether SAE features are reproducible. It does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses polysemanticity as motivation and reports functional SAE evaluations, but those are not results about the listed claim versions. Feature-correspondence measurements in Tables 2 and 25 bear on V5's stability component. The study does not assess whether SAE features are complete or canonical in the model.
record.test_reason: It measures one-to-one Hungarian feature correspondence between reduced-data SAEs (5M to 50M tokens) and a 500M-token reference, across three LLMs and two SAE types. That bears directly on the stability part of V5. It does not test toy models, capacity, or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Functional SAE metrics often reach 500M-reference levels at small budgets, but one-to-one feature reproducibility keeps improving with data. Counterpart agreement emerges before strong alignment. Data needs depend on the objective, and feature-level claims need explicit reproducibility checks.
record.recipe_differences: This SAE data-budget and feature-correspondence study does not implement the toy-network superposition method; it compares trained SAE dictionaries against a 500M-token reference.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature correspondence changes with activation budget, SAE architecture, and the strictness of the cosine threshold.
record.problems: The feature correspondence tables report no uncertainty estimates. The 500M-token SAE is a reference, not evidence that its features are canonical. The authors note that the study relies heavily on SAEBench training and evaluation implementations.
record.rows_left_out: Functional SAE metrics and activation-selection comparisons were not included because they do not measure any of the claim versions. No relevant feature-correspondence results were omitted.

untested.parts: Completeness and canonicality of SAE features. Reproducibility across seeds or independent datasets at the same budget: no 500M-vs-500M seed control is reported, so data-budget effects cannot be separated from seed variance.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or recoverable by SAEs is assumed, not tested.
Entire version: feature dimensionality is not examined.

missing.what: Shared-feature fractions at the looser thresholds τ≥0.3 and τ≥0.5. Example: Qwen3-8B BatchTopK at 50M is 72.78% (τ≥0.3) and 49.49% (τ≥0.5). These show the result depends on the threshold choice.
Mean matched decoder cosine similarity of 0.454 for Gemma-2-2B BatchTopK at 5M.
Qualitative matched pairs: low- and medium-alignment matched latents carry different semantic descriptions, while high-alignment pairs match.

record.verdict_notes: The reference is a single 500M SAE, and no seed-to-seed baseline at equal budget is given. Low correspondence therefore mixes data-budget effects with ordinary seed instability (cf. Paulo & Belrose). No uncertainty is reported for the correspondence tables. Functional SAEBench results were rightly excluded because they do not measure any version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, and sparsity-dependent geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes neuron polysemanticity or causes important features to receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or are sparse features recoverable by an SAE; the paper evaluates SAE data requirements, not those claims.
Completeness and canonicality of SAE features, and reproducibility across seeds or independently sampled datasets at the same budget.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional. The study compares feature-direction cosine similarities but does not test feature dimensionality or superposition.

relationships.condition: ReLU SAEs trained on 5M–50M tokens vs the 500M reference (Gemma-2-2B 65k, Qwen3-8B, Pythia-160M)
relationships.reason: Encoder–decoder counterpart agreement is 70–85%, but strict shared features at τ=0.7 are only 18.6–47.3%. Feature identity depends on training-data budget (r1–r6, r13–r18, r25–r30).
relationships.display_finding: Encoder–decoder counterpart agreement was 70–85%, but only 18.6–47.3% of features were strictly shared at τ=0.7.

source_check.reason: Tables 2 and 25 show incomplete, budget-dependent correspondence: strict shared-feature fractions range from 18.58% to 47.26%, qualifying feature stability.

relationships.condition: BatchTopK SAEs trained on 5M–50M tokens vs the 500M reference (Gemma-2-2B 16k, Qwen3-8B, Pythia-160M)
relationships.reason: Strict shared features at τ=0.7 are only 1.1–2.2% at 5M and at most 28.9% at 50M, even though counterpart agreement is 47–85%. Feature reproducibility depends strongly on budget and architecture (r7–r12, r19–r24, r31–r36).
relationships.display_finding: Only 1.1–2.2% of features were strictly shared at 5M tokens and at most 28.9% at 50M, despite 47–85% counterpart agreement.

relation.reason: One-to-one feature correspondence across training-data budgets directly tests the stability component of V5.

tranche.reason: The claim-relevant results qualify V5: individual SAE features remain incompletely reproducible and their correspondence depends on activation budget, even when functional metrics approach the reference.

source_check.notes: Appendix A specifies Qwen3-8B width 65,536; Table 25 leaves Pythia width unspecified despite both widths being trained. No same-budget reference-seed control is reported; counterpart agreement does not establish strong directional recovery, and completeness is untested.
